newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm Oil/Laurics -- Palm prices seen staying firm.
newsitem.headline: Palm Oil/Laurics -- Palm prices seen staying firm.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm oil prices are expected to stay firm this week on the back of increased exports and tight supply, regional traders say.
Coconut oil prices, however, are seen softening due to poor local demand, they say.
Traders say the prospect of further export business to India and fresh demand from China should underpin market sentiment.
Total palm oil exports from Malaysia and Indonesia to India in August are estimated to be more than 200,000 tonnes.
India imported 113,000 tonnes in July, traders said.
"India has been an active export market and this has largely helped boost regional prices," said one Malaysian trader.

India's State Trading Corporation (STC) was rumored to be in the market for up to 250,000 tonnes of palm oil for September/October shipment, but this was denied by an STC official in Singapore on Friday.
Traders said last week's news that China had approved imports of 1.3 million tonnes of palm oil between August 1996 and March 1997 would continue to have a positive impact on prices.
While the news may have been factored into the market, they said China's incremental purchase of the palm oil under the quota will help support prices.

Traders said the improving demand had also dispelled concerns that palm oil stocks in Malaysia could reach one million tonnes this year. Stocks at the end of July stood at 754,634 tonnes, according to official Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority estimates.
Benchmark third position November crude palm oil futures closed on Friday at 1,196 ringgit a tonne after hitting a high of 1,200, against 1,149 a week earlier.
Indonesian traders expect firm domestic crude palm oil and palm olein prices to continue until the end of August.
"The supply is still tight and I don't think prices will ease (this) week. Many dealers have already engaged in export contracts following low export taxes," one trader said.

"We just wait and see what the National Logistic Agency (BULOG) would do to control prices. They might want to launch fresh market operations again, but the problem is palm oil supply is very tight at present," he said.
On Friday, ready palm olein was quoted at 1,550-80 rupiah/kg in Jakarta and Surabaya, while olein in Medan edged up to 1,470 rupiah from 1,460 in the morning.
Traders said a tender of 2,000 tonnes of crude palm oil was sold at 1,215 rupiah a kg on Thursday, compared with 1,175 rupiah on Tuesday.
Philippine traders said continued lack of local demand could weigh on coconut oil prices this week.
"Prices will soften a little because local demand is not improving even with the slight increase in supply," said one trader.
Traders said speculation on the arrival of a ship carrying 37,000 tonnes of coconut oil from the Philippines may also affect prices. The ship is scheduled to arrive in Rotterdam on September 2.
"If it arrives on time, coconut oil prices for nearby months may come down by $30 and prices on forward months by $10," said one trader.
The July-August contract was last traded at $780 on Thursday from $777.50 at the start of the week.
Contracts on the commodity on its way to Rotterdam were last traded at $920 per tonne, traders said.
